entry.title: CDC funding for HIV prevention shifted from providers to states under Trump
entry.summary: Nonprofits fighting HIV used get direct funding from the CDC. Now that money is going to state health departments that may have other priorities.

entry.title: An early start to flu season moves up vaccination timing
entry.summary: This year's flu season is unusual. It started early and in the West, instead of the South. A new variant with a mutation that helps the virus evade immunity may be playing a role.

entry.title: What happened during Christa Pike's failed execution
entry.summary: Catherine Sweeney was in the witness room when Tennessee attempted to execute Christa Pike on Sept. 30. An attempted execution in May had also failed. Here's what Sweeney saw and heard.

entry.title: Wildfire smoke affects animals in unique ways. Scientists are trying to understand it
entry.summary: The new field of "smoke ecology" examines how wildfire smoke perturbs wild places and animals — and what might be done to prevent its worst mayhem.

entry.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating them now.

entry.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
entry.summary: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.

entry.title: What does marathon training do to your body? A reporter becomes the test subject
entry.summary: Before running the New York City Marathon, NPR's Elissa Nadworny gets a bone scan, blood work and a treadmill test to settle a question from Mom: Is this bad for my body?

entry.title: 4 ways to battle performance anxiety, according to a confidence coach
entry.summary: Worried about stumbling before a high-stakes event, like a race or a job interview? Psychologist Cindra Kamphoff offers creative strategies to overcome the jitters and build confidence in the moment.

entry.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
entry.summary: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.

entry.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
entry.summary: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.
